intro: This video shows how the second example project of Open E Craft is drawn: a start and stop circuit, with a relay that holds itself through its own contact. We use the web editor again, so there is nothing to install.
new: Start with New project, and open its page. On the View tab, Fit page shows the whole sheet. Zoom in two steps, and drag with the right mouse button to move the page.
pot24: The potentials come from the Insert center on the right. Search for the potential plus 24 volts and click it. The R key turns the symbol while you place it. Escape ends placing.
pot0: 0 volts goes to the bottom in the same way, turned with R as well, so that both arrows point along their rails.
rails: The wire tool is on the Insert tab. Click the start of a wire and its end, and press Enter. Both potentials get a rail: every wire that touches it carries its potential.
breaker: Devices come from the parts database, so each one brings its symbol and its part. Search for the miniature circuit breaker, turn it upright again with R, and place it. It gets the tag F 1 by itself.
terminal1: The push buttons sit in the cabinet door, so their wires run through terminals. Place a feed-through terminal. It becomes terminal 1 of the strip X 1.
buttons: Below it, the red push button with a normally closed contact stops the machine, and the green one starts it. They get the tags S 1 and S 2. Symbols in line are connected by the editor.
terminal2: A second terminal leads back into the cabinet. It gets the number 2 by itself.
coil: Now the relay: a contactor with a coil for 24 volts. Its coil becomes K 1.
wires1: Three wires are still missing. The W key starts the wire tool as well. From the rail to the circuit breaker, on to the first terminal, and from the coil down to 0 volts. Where a wire meets a rail, the editor sets a junction.
accessory: A relay is more than its coil. Select the coil and open the Parts tab of the Properties pane. Add accessory offers the auxiliary contact blocks that fit this contactor. Choose the one with two normally open and two normally closed contacts. Now K 1 has two parts.
unplaced: Now search for K 1 in the Insert center. Under Unplaced, it lists the contacts of the parts that are not in the schematic yet. Click the normally open contact 13, 14, and place it beside the start button.
hold: Two wires put it in parallel to the start button. This is the self-holding: once the relay has picked up, its own contact keeps the coil energised, until the stop button opens the circuit.
lamp1: Two more contacts of K 1 switch the indicator lamps. The normally open contact 53, 54, a terminal, and the green lamp from the parts database show that the machine is on. They are in line, so the editor wires them together.
lamp2: The normally closed contact 61, 62, another terminal, and the red lamp show that it is off. The terminals count on by themselves, 3 and 4, and the lamps are P 1 and P 2.
wires2: Four wires connect the two lamp circuits to the rails. At the end of a rail, the wire simply turns the corner. And all wires take the colour of their potential: blue, for a control circuit with direct current.
closeup: Hold Control and turn the mouse wheel for a closer look. Coil and contacts are one device. Every contact shows where its coil is: on page 1, in column 2. And below the coil, the contact image lists each contact with the place where it is used. The main contacts and two contacts of the auxiliary block are left as a reserve.
text: Select a device to edit it in the Properties pane. On its Device tab, the push buttons get the function texts Stop and Start. They appear beside the symbols, and in the reports.
numbers: On the Connections tab, Wire numbering numbers all connections. With the scheme page and column, a number tells where to find its wire: the first one in column 2 of page 1 is 1 dot 2 dot 1.
check: The status bar shows the project check, which follows every change: no errors and no warnings.
terminals: The terminal strip was never drawn as such, and still the editor knows it. On the Project data tab, Reports has the terminal diagram of X 1, with the wires on both sides of each terminal. Insert as report page makes it a page of the project.
connections: The connection list is made the same way: every wire with its number, both ends, its colour and its cross-section. The cabinet could be wired from this list alone.
pages: Both are pages of the project now, and they stay up to date when the circuit changes.
outro: Back on the schematic page, the start and stop circuit is complete. You find this example and sixteen more on the start page of the editor. Open E Craft is free and open source, at open e craft dot org.
